newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Imation says to penetrate deeper into Asia.
newsitem.headline: Imation says to penetrate deeper into Asia.

text.p: Imation Corp's chairman and chief executive officer, William Monahan, said on Thursday he sees the U.S. imaging and information company gaining a deeper foothold in the Asia-Pacific region.

The company, a spin-off of Minnesota Mining & Manufacturing Co (3M) data storage and imaging systems units, wants its international business outside the U.S. to grow to over 60 percent of its total global business towards the year 2000, from 50 percent now, Monahan said.
"We see the fastest growing areas of our company to be in the international environment with the leading growth priority in Asia," Monahan told a news conference.
"Asia-Pacific is our second largest international market. We expect it to grow at better than 25 percent in coming years."
South Asia and China are Imation's key targets. Others included Indonesia, India, Singapore, Thailand and Malaysia, said vice-president of international operations David Wenck.

In India, the company is planning new sales offices in Madras and Calcutta in addition to existing ones in Bombay, New Delhi and Bangalore. Imation aims to grow "dramatically in all core businesses" -- printing and publishing, medical imaging, data storage and service organisation -- in Asia, Monahan said.
"We feel we have been under-penetrated in Asia and Latin America in the past. That has changed," Monahan said.

"We believe the best strategy to carry us into the future is the delivery of proprietary products -- products that add more value than our competitors," said Monahan, adding that Eastman Kodak, Agfa-Gevaert and Fuji were some of Imation's main competitors.
Other strategies cited included tie-ups with key Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) and strategic partners.
Monahan said Imation was already working closely with Seagate Technology in drive manufacture, and also with Acer, Hewlett Packard and Toshiba.
Aggressive promotions and advertising campaigns to promote its LS-120 drives were also among plans to gain market share.
LS-120 drives are high capacity three-and-a-half inch diskettes with 120 megabytes.
Imation is poised to increase its LS-120 drive capacity in 1997 to over 500,000 units from 60,000 in December. The rise in production was scheduled from the second quarter onwards.
Medical imaging contributes about 25 percent to Imation's total revenue while printing and publishing another 25 percent, data storage 40 percent and service organisation 10 percent.
